Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:23: Now, the arguments he says to his heart are two: the first, that were it not for His love, He would not have chastised us, for otherwise He would have annihilated us; this is proof that He chastised us out of love, as it says (Psalms 118:18) "the Lord has chastened me severely." The second: He renews the act of Creation every single day continually, which is complete kindness, and how much more so will He fulfill His word, which He spoke by the hand of His servants the prophets, to gather us from the four corners of the earth - so far. When you examine his words, you will find them close to my teacher's view that we have written, concerning the reason why one who acts from love merits the supernal pleasantness, as we have explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:24: On the Mishnah "any love dependent on something, when the thing ceases, the love ceases" - he writes: it hints that one who serves the Name, blessed be He, so that his possessions increase and his soul be preserved, his service is not complete, as Satan said (Job 1:9) "does Job fear God for nothing? Have You not made a hedge about him?" To this the Tanna [teacher] says that one who serves the Name for the sake of physical things upon which he has made his service dependent, his service will not endure to illuminate with the light of life, for once those things upon which his service depends cease, his love ceases - and there is no eating or drinking in Sheol, where you are going. But one who serves the Name with complete love, behold, his love is in the life of the worlds, and never departs, and his reward is that he shall love the Name forever, as it says, "and their crowns are on their heads and they delight in the radiance of the Shechinah" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:25: The Tanna explains and says, "what is love that does not depend on something? This is the love of David and Jonathan." The intent is that it is said of them (I Samuel 18:1) "and it came to pass, when he had finished speaking, that the soul of Jonathan was bound to the soul of David," etc.; and likewise it is said (ibid. 20:41) "and they kissed one another and wept, one with another, until David exceeded" - and there is no kissing except from the side of love, and weeping from the side of cleaving; and "until David exceeded" is because it is the secret of the exile of the Shechinah, and David and Jonathan hint at the secret of love in the secret of "love-tokens" [dodim] above - and the discerning reader will understand.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:26: In the Zohar, they explain a hidden and concealed secret concerning the matter of love; we shall quote his words - his words (Shemot 146a): concerning what it says (Song of Songs 1:2) "let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth" - what did Solomon the king see, that he brought words of love between the upper world and the lower world, and the beginning of the praise of love that he introduced between them is "let him kiss me"? Rather, it has already been established, and this is so: there is no love of cleaving, spirit with spirit, except through a kiss, and a kiss is on the mouth, the source of the spirit and its emission; and when they kiss, one another, these spirits become bound one with another and become one - and then it is a single love. In the book of Rav Hamnuna Sabba, the first, he used to say concerning this verse: the kiss of love spreads into four spirits, and the four spirits are as one, and they are within the secret of faith, and they ascend through four letters, and these letters, upon which the holy Name depends, upper and lower depend upon them, and the praise of the Song of Songs depends upon them - and what is it? Love. And they are the supernal Chariot, and they are fellowship and cleaving and the completeness of everything - these are the four letters, four spirits, and they are the spirits of love and joy of all the limbs of the body, without any sadness at all - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:27: My teacher, peace be upon him, explains this passage in his commentary on the Sabba (Zohar, Mishpatim 124b), and likewise in the Zohar in the portion mentioned. Let us explain what pertains to our discourse concerning love: that the reality of the merit of love is the bond of four spirits, made in the secret of the kisses, and the secret of the kisses is explained there, further on in the portion - "who will kiss me" - that which is concealed within the supernal concealment; and the secret of the kiss is the cleaving of the inner essence of the sefirot and their inwardness, which is the spirit of life that gives them life, and this is what it says, "and a kiss is on the mouth, which is the source of the spirit and its emission"; and likewise it says (Zohar Chadash, Shir HaShirim 63a) that in the Song of Songs, cleaving of body to body means "let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth" - cleaving of spirit to spirit - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:28: How there are four spirits is explained there in the Song of Songs (Zohar Chadash, Shir HaShirim 64a) - their words: "'let him kiss me' - cleaving in love, spirit with spirit, for four spirits join and become as one - this one gives its spirit to its fellow and takes the spirit of its fellow, which cleaves to it - so there is his own spirit and his fellow's spirit, that makes two, and likewise his fellow - thus there are four spirits joined together in those kisses" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:29: He says at the end of the passage we quoted: "and they are the spirits of love and joy of all the limbs of the body, without any sadness at all." The meaning is that it is impossible for them to cleave in the inner spirit unless the sefirot are bound together as one from the side of their externality, and judgment, which is their sadness, is diminished from them - then it becomes a throne for the supernal spirit to rest upon them. It is like the parable of a man kissing his beloved, who kisses her only out of great joy, when all his limbs have already been unified as one - and this is the word "ahavah" [love], which sums to "echad" [one, numerically], indicating the bond and union of the caused, created beings, one with another, through their inner spirit and soul.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:30: He explains in the passage also that the letters of "ahavah" are letters upon which the holy Name depends, and these are the letters of the Name YHVH; and my teacher, peace be upon him, writes and ascribes a relationship between the letters of "ahavah" and the letters of YHVH, and with this we understand why in most verses of the Torah it is written "to love YHVH."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:31: Now we must understand how, in the reality of a person's love for the Holy One, blessed be He, four spirits are found. The matter is that a person's soul is a portion of God above, and when a person prepares his body and limbs together and arouses his heart in joy - for the Shechinah does not rest amid sadness - and intends to arouse love of his Maker within his heart, then a supernal spirit is necessarily aroused within his heart, and a holy flow is drawn into it - that makes two; and this is the matter of "let him kiss me," that the spirit of the masculine comes down below to make kisses; and afterward he intends to comprise and cleave his soul above - that makes two spirits above. This reality of the two is made of itself, like the "face answers to face" I explained above, and thereby the love becomes complete - four spirits joined together as one.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:32: The matter is further explained in the words of Rashbi (Zohar, Pekudei 226b) - his words: "this sixth Palace is kisses, to cleave spirit to spirit, lower to upper, as it says (Song of Songs 1:2) 'let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth,' and every kiss is to cleave spirit to spirit, upper to lower." And he says further on: "and this secret: when spirit is unified with spirit, then the kisses begin to join, and the rest of the limbs are aroused in repentance, and this spirit cleaves to that one, and then all the limbs are aroused, one with another, to bind limb to limb; and if you should say, who arouses the lower limbs or the upper limbs - the lower limbs are always aroused toward the upper, whoever is in darkness always longs to be in light, the black flame below is always aroused toward the white flame above, in order to cleave to it and rest beneath it, and this is the secret of (Psalms 83:2) 'God, do not be silent; do not hold Your peace, and do not be still, O God'" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:33: Although at first glance it appears that this passage disagrees with what is explained in the Song of Songs, which says that kisses are the cleaving of the supernal spirit in the lower, this is not a difficulty - for the intent of this passage in the portion of Pekudei, which says that kisses are to cleave spirit to spirit, lower to upper, means that the yearning of the lower spirit is to be comprised in the upper, and this is what "let him kiss me" means - that the lower spirit be comprised in the upper. But it is impossible for the lower to be comprised in the upper unless the kiss of the masculine comes and its spirit is comprised in it, and through the striking of that illumination, power is given to the lower spirit to be comprised in the upper; and in order for that illumination to come from the masculine, the arousal of the female must precede it first, as it is written, "the lower limbs are always aroused toward the upper."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:34: Along these lines is the reality of love in man: first, one's yearnings must precede, to cleave to the supernal light, and once the Holy One, blessed be He, sees his yearning shining forth [being revealed] within him from His supernal light, through this his soul too is comprised above, and four spirits are found bound together as one above - a doubled bond in reality, like the "face answers to face" I explained in chapter 1, that when a person arouses love of his fellow within his heart, his fellow too arouses his love for him in his heart, and so two spirits are found in each - this is the secret of Rabbi Yosi's words, "spirit draws spirit and brings spirit," which I explained in chapter 1.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:35: With this we also understand what they say (Yoma 39a), "one who sanctifies himself a little is sanctified a great deal," for the bond is doubled as we explained, and he cannot quickly be separated from the sanctity of his love of Him, blessed be He, since the King has also taken hold of him with cords of love, and therefore he is sanctified greatly - like the parable of one who ties his fellow with a rope to bring him near, and once his fellow sees that he wishes to bind him, he too casts a rope toward him, and they draw near to one another quickly and are bound in a single, strong, mighty bond, between which there is no separation at all.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:36: Whoever merits this love is, without doubt, bound and cleaved to the supernal life, and happy is he in this world and the World to Come. Concerning this it is said (Deuteronomy 30:20) "to love the Lord and to cleave to Him," and this is the secret of (Deuteronomy 4:4) "but you who cleave to the Lord your God are all alive today," as I explained in chapter 1.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:37: This is likewise explained in the Zohar (Mishpatim 124b), on the verse "but you who cleave" - concerning the secret of kisses - their words: "and therefore it is written 'let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth,' for this is cleaving, spirit with spirit. We learn: whenever the Holy One, blessed be He, goes with Israel, as it were, spirit cleaves to spirit, and therefore it is written (Deuteronomy 4:4) 'but you who cleave to the Lord your God,' in all those kinds of cleaving, and this is not separated from that" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:38: Now that we have explained that love is the kisses, it is fitting to explain whether they are found in Binah and in Chesed. Kisses found in Binah are explained in the Song of Songs (Zohar Chadash 64a) - their words: "'from the kisses' - from those supernal kisses that were kissed beforehand, for the love of joy is only from within kisses, the cleaving of the supernal spirit in the lower. 'His mouth' [pihu], not written 'his mouth' [piv, standard form] - what is 'pihu'? Rather, an invitation of the World to Come, the King to whom all peace belongs, and this is the added Heh added to this [word], because all the love of the lower world is only to become joined with the upper world, the World to Come, and therefore all praises arouse the lower world toward the upper world" - so far, their words. Here it is explained that kisses are from the side of the supernal Heh, the World to Come.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:39: That kisses are an arousal from the side of Chesed is explained there in the portion of Terumah - their words: "once he enters the Palace of love, the love of supernal kisses is aroused, as it is written 'and Jacob kissed Rachel,' to make the kisses of supernal love as is fitting; and these kisses are the beginning of the arousal of all the love of cleaving and bonding above" - so far. It is necessarily inferred from the context of this passage's wording that this mentioned Palace of Love is Chesed within Atzilut, and so my teacher, peace be upon him, explains, saying that from it the love of kisses is aroused.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:40: It remains now to explain what is explained in the Zohar, that love is from the side of the supernal Mother. The reason is that when a person considers the abundant goodness of the Creator, blessed be He, toward him, which cannot be counted, one part in a thousand of His goodness to us in the matter of our creation, his soul yearns to serve Him from love, as our Sages, of blessed memory, say in the Tanchuma (see Emor, 7), on the verse (Job 41:3) "who has preceded Me, that I should repay him?" - their words: Rabbi Yirmiyah ben Elazar said, in the future a Heavenly Voice will burst forth on the mountaintops and say, "whoever has worked with God, let him come and take his reward," and the Holy Spirit cries out and says, "who has preceded Me, that I should repay him? Who praised Me before I gave him a soul? Who circumcised before I gave him a son? Who made tzitzit before I gave him a tallit? Who made a parapet before I gave him a roof?" - and they elaborate further there similarly on every matter - "I must repay him." Why? "Under the whole heaven is Mine" - for everything is Mine, and from what is Mine I give to him, and yet, "and I shall repay" - I must repay him - so far. This midrash is quoted in Vayikra Rabbah, portion "an ox or a sheep" (27:2), see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:41: When we consider the words of this passage along the secret way, "Mi" [who] is the Mother, corresponding to the fifty gates of Binah that spread from her to do good to all creatures, as told in the reply, "and the Lord answered Job out of the whirlwind" (38:1), which mentions fifty gates there: "who [mi] has set its measurements, if you know"; or "who has stretched the line upon it"; "who has divided a channel for the torrent" (ibid. 25); or "who has begotten the drops of dew" (ibid. 28); "from whose womb has the ice come forth" (ibid. 29); "who provides for the raven its prey" (ibid. 41); "who has sent out the wild donkey free" (ibid. 39:5) - in sum, fifty gates are mentioned there, as the Ra'avad, peace be upon him, explains in his commentary on Sefer Yetzirah (introduction). We find, then, that the Holy One, blessed be He, preceded and opened fifty gates of His goodness to do good to all creatures, and therefore He says, "who has preceded Me" - for by the attribute of "Mi" no creature preceded Me; rather, "Mi" preceded and gave him a soul and all good things - this is why Binah is called "Kedem" [before/ancient], and she preceded the world, as our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer, chapter 3), among the seven things created before the world was created, one of them being the Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 8:22) "the Lord made me as the beginning of His way, before His works of old" - and it says "before," meaning before the world was created. And likewise the Garden of Eden, as it is said (Genesis 2:8) "a garden in Eden, from before [mikedem]" - before the world was created; and this is because "olam" [world] refers to the six directions, and that which precedes the six-directional world is Binah, and therefore she is called "Kedem," as Rabbi Moshe de Leon and my teacher, in Sefer Pardes Rimonim, explain. And nevertheless, "I must repay" - for the good reward of the righteous is to behold the pleasantness of the Lord flowing from her, and this is "I must repay" - along the lines of "al HaShem" (Zohar III 79b, on the verse I Samuel 1:10).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:42: Concerning our discourse, in which we explained that love flows from the Mother, who is Heh: when a person considers that the Holy One, blessed be He, created him and depicted and stamped his body and spirit with the twenty-two holy letters, which are from the side of the Mother, and by them is the mold of all the worlds, it is fitting that he love Him and do His will - especially since she is the Mother who bestows good kindnesses upon her children, as is explained in Sefer HaBahir (see 105). This is Heh - the five lights of the first day, as explained in the Tikkunim (4b, 19a), which come to Chesed, and are the root of the fifty gates; and likewise in the Zohar (Vayetze 154a) and the Song of Songs (Zohar Chadash 62a), they elaborate on the matter of Binah, that she is a place that requires joy, where there is no anger or judgment, for the World to Come is entirely joy, and she rejoices for all, sending forth joy and gladness in every direction - so far. And so she is a river that flows and issues forth, and its waters never cease (Zohar, Bereishit 33b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 2:43: Further, in another aspect, love should rightly be ascribed to Binah, because through the answering of our prayer in all our troubles, as it is written (Deuteronomy 4:7) "for what great nation is there that has God so near to it, as the Lord our God is, whenever we call upon Him?" And it is explained in the Zohar, portion of Va'etchanan (265a), that there is a distinction between "the Lord your God" and "the Lord our God" - "the Lord your God" refers to the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, while "the Lord our God" refers to Abba and Imma. We find, then, that fear is that a person fear the Emanator, who is the Creator of everything, great and ruling, and this fear of His is revealed to a person through Abba, as we explained in the Gate of Fear, chapter 2; and love is that a person love the Creator of everything from the side of His kindnesses and His goodness toward him, and the revelation of this love to a person is revealed through Imma, as we explained; and the essence of love is the arousal of the heart in yearning, as will be further explained, with the Lord's help. So too they say, of blessed memory, in Tractate Kallah (chapter 3): what is love and what is honor? Love is in the heart, and honor is in deeds and words - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:1: Although the essence of love has been explained in the previous chapters, it still remains to explain further its essence and how a person may cleave to it in such a way that it never departs from him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:2: Concerning the essence of love, Rashbi, peace be upon him, further explains - his words (Zohar, Acharei Mot 67a): Rabbi Abba said, (Isaiah 26:9) "my soul desires You in the night, my spirit within me also seeks You early" - "desires You" - it should say "You," "seeks You" - it should say "will seek You" [in the future form]; rather, it has already been established, as it says (Job 12:10) "in whose hand is the soul of every living thing and the breath of all mankind." Come and see, nefesh and ruach have always been joined together; we learn, the complete service that a person must render to the Holy One, blessed be He, is as we learn (Deuteronomy 6:5) "and you shall love the Lord your God" - that he love the Holy One, blessed be He, with the love of the soul truly, and this is complete love, the love of his soul and spirit; just as these cleave to the body, and the body loves them, so a person must cleave to love the Holy One, blessed be He, with the love of his soul and spirit, to cleave to Him - this is [the meaning of] "my soul desires You in the night" - meaning, my soul truly; "my spirit within me also seeks You early" - to cleave to You with abundant love.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:3: "In the night" - for a person, out of love for the Holy One, blessed be He, must rise every night to engage in His service, until morning breaks and a thread of kindness is drawn upon him, for we learn: happy is the portion of that person who loves the Holy One, blessed be He, with this love - and these are the truly righteous, who love the Holy One, blessed be He, thus, since the world endures for their sake, and they rule over all the harsh decrees above and below, since the world endures for their sake; we learn, that righteous one who cleaves with his spirit and soul above, to the Holy King, in love as is fitting, rules over the earth below, and everything he decrees upon the world endures - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:4: The interpretation of "desires You" [avitecha] - it should say "You" [otecha] - the intent is that the plain sense of the verse seems to say that the soul desires the Holy One, blessed be He, at night, and through the spirit within him he seeks Him early in the morning; and he raises a difficulty: since "desires You" and "seeks You" refer back to nefesh and ruach, it should say "my nefesh [desires] You" and "my ruach seeks You" [in a form implying reciprocity]. To this he answers that "my nefesh" and "my ruach" do not refer only to the nefesh and ruach of a person, but also to the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, who are also called nefesh and ruach, since from them come [human] nefesh and ruach, as he writes further on: "come and see, nefesh and ruach have always been joined" - the reason being that they are joined in the world because their root comes from above, from the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah, and one without the other is impossible, as it is said (Psalms 89:15) "righteousness and justice are the foundation of Your throne" - so the branches coming from them are joined. Therefore they say in the Tikkunim (49b), on the verse (Proverbs 20:27) "the candle of the Lord is the soul of man" - Ner: Nefesh, Ruach; Nishmat: Neshamah - we find nefesh and ruach joined together.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:5: He brings the verse "in whose hand is the soul of every living thing" to show that even though the ruach and nefesh descend and are clothed in the body, their root remains above, and through that root remaining there, He truly has in His hand the soul of every living thing - and this matter is a preface to the matter of love that he explains afterward, and to resolve the difficulty of "desires You" - it should say "You" - to this he says that if the intent were the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah alone, it should say "O Lord, my God, I desire You in the night, my spirit also seeks You"; rather, to teach us the matter of love and the cleaving of a person's soul to the Holy One, blessed be He, and how it is, he says "my soul and my spirit."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:6: Further, he intended to bring this verse also to resolve what the verse says, "my spirit within me also seeks You early" - according to his interpretation, which refers back to the Holy One, blessed be He, it should say "my spirit also seeks You," for the word "within me" [bekirbi] is superfluous; to this he intended to bring this verse, "in whose hand," to show that truly a spark of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah is within a person, and souls are threads of flame drawn from above to below, and they live only from their root, which flows into them always; and once the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to remove support from the lower nefesh and ruach, He removes the root bound with it, so that it does not bestow life upon the lower nefesh and ruach, and immediately the person dies, as it is written (Job 34:14-15) "if He should gather to Himself his spirit and his soul, all flesh would perish together" - and "gathering" is this, that He gathers his spirit to Himself, like one who smells an apple and the like, drawing that scent [spirit] and gathering it to himself - so the spirit and soul are gathered to their source.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:7: This is likewise explained by Rashbi (Zohar, Vayechi 217b): Rabbi Yehudah said, happy are the righteous when the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to return his spirit to Him, to draw that spirit within Himself, for we learn, at the time the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to return his spirit to Him, if he is righteous, what is written? (Ecclesiastes 12:7) "and the spirit returns to God who gave it" - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:8: We find, then, that while a person is alive, a spirit of life from the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah is within him, giving him life, and this is "in whose hand is the soul of every living thing," bestowing life - He removes it all as He wills. With this the word "within me" [bekirbi] is resolved, this word referring both to the nefesh and to the ruach emanated from the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah. The wording of the verse is thus: "my soul desires You in the night, my spirit also" - referring to the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shechinah - "within me" - "seeks You early." And "seeks You early" means to engage in His service until morning breaks, as will be explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:9: Now, with this introduction, we understand the verse (Deuteronomy 32:9) "for the Lord's portion is His people, Jacob the lot of His inheritance." We must understand what "portion" means and what "lot [cord]" means, and why it says "His people" and not "Israel." It may be understood by what we have explained: that when we say "portion," it indicates that souls are hewn from Him, and He and they are two portions, like two halves of a body, and this is the nature of the word "portion" - that a thing is divided from itself; and when the portion of the lower soul is united with Him, the two portions become unified and made one. And although it says "portions," which would indicate, God forbid, separation, the intent is not that the soul is separated from Him upon its descent below, but rather that its root remains there, and therefore it says "His people" - precisely His own people is the portion - and therefore it does not say "for the Lord's portion is Israel," which would indicate that the portion was divided below and would indicate separation, but rather "His people" - meaning that His people are truly His. And to indicate the doubled bond, He too, blessed be He, flows a spark of life to the lower spirit and soul in the body, and never separates - therefore it says "Jacob the lot [chevel] of His inheritance," for just as a rope [chevel] is woven from two or three strands, so He is bound with us below, and we are bound with Him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:10: Further, in the parable of the rope, our Sages, of blessed memory, explain (Bemidbar Rabbah 17:6) a pleasant matter concerning the mitzvot, and we quoted their words in the chapter and Gate 1 of the Gate of Commandments, where it says: a parable of one cast into the water; the captain [ship's guide] extended a rope to him and said to him, "take hold of this rope in your hand and do not let go of it, for if you let go you have no life." So too, the reality of the soul is lowered from above to below like this rope - one end in His hand and the other end in a person's body - and the whole reality of love and cleaving is to cleave to this rope and bind oneself to the root of one's soul, which is bound to Him, blessed be He.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:11: With this we understand the wording of the passage: "we learn, the complete service that a person must render to the Holy One, blessed be He, is as we learn, 'and you shall love the Lord your God' - that he love the Holy One, blessed be He, with the love of the soul truly, just as these cleave to the body, and the body loves them, so a person must cleave," etc. The meaning is that the verse (Deuteronomy 6:5) says "and you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul" - that he love Him with the love of the soul truly, and its explanation is that the love of the soul with the body is a doubled love, for the soul loves the body and the body loves the soul, and they do not wish to be separated one from the other.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:12: The love of the soul for the body is taught to us by Scripture in saying (Song of Songs 8:6) "for love is as strong as death," and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Vayechi 245a) that at the time of a person's death, the soul is asked to leave the body like a person going on a long journey, separating from his beloved, for whom the separation is hard - his words: "'set me as a seal upon your heart' - so that your whole image remain in you, like this seal whose whole image remains in the place to which it is affixed; 'for love is as strong as death' - it is as mighty as the separation of the spirit from the body, for we learn: at the time a person is about to depart the world and sees what he sees, the spirit goes through all the limbs of the body and rolls its wheels as one who travels on the sea without oars, going up and down, and it avails him nothing; it comes and is drawn away from all the limbs of the body, and there is no strength like that of the day the spirit separates from the body - the strength of the love of Knesset Yisrael for the Holy One, blessed be He, is like the strength of death at the time the spirit wishes to separate from the body."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:13: "Jealousy is cruel as Sheol" - whoever loves and is not bound to Him with jealousy, his love is not true love; once he is jealous, behold, his love is complete. From this we learn that a person must be jealous for his wife, so that a complete love be bound with her, for through this he will not set his eyes on another woman. What is "jealousy is cruel as Sheol"? Just as Sheol is harsh in the eyes of the wicked who must descend into it, so jealousy is harsh in the eyes of one who loves and is jealous, at being separated from his love - so far.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:14: This is what he says in the passage before us: "just as these cleave to the body" - this is the love of the soul for the body, which is cleaved to it and does not wish to be separated from it, since after being clothed in it, it has a relationship and closeness with it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:15: "And the body loves them" - this is the love of the body, since it has no life except through it [the soul]; just as it is hard, in the eyes of the Shechinah, to be separated from the Holy One, blessed be He, so much that she says "set me as a seal," in the same reality that it is hard for the spirit to separate from the body - such a love the souls of the righteous must have with the Shechinah, and this is what he says, "then he must cleave" - in this same reality, he loves the Holy One, blessed be He, with the love of his soul and spirit, to cleave to Him; just as he loves his own spirit and soul within his body, which gives him life, so he should love the Holy One, blessed be He, and cleave to Him with the portion of his lower spirit and soul, for in truth they only live through the flow of the supernal roots cleaving to Him, blessed be He, through which He sends life to the lower branches in the body, as we have explained. And so he says at the end of the passage, "that righteous one who cleaves with his spirit and his soul above to the Holy King."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:16: Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains, in the passage from Vayechi we quoted, that among the signs of love is jealousy, and he explains that one who is jealous for his wife, out of his great love for her, does not wish a stranger to enter between them to separate him from her, but rather that his wife's love be bound to him forever - so too the righteous man must, out of his great love for the Shechinah, become so bound in love of her that he becomes jealous for her, not wishing the Shechinah to separate from him and rest upon another, in such a way that she be uprooted from him - and this is the reality of "the love of his soul and spirit, to cleave." And the indication of this reality of love is that he rises at night to engage in Torah, as he explains further on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:17: The second aspect, which is the love of the soul for the body, is likewise self-explained, for certainly the Holy One, blessed be He, loves it, since He gives it the soul from Himself so that it may live; and it is fitting for a person to say in his heart, "just as the Holy One, blessed be He, desires to cleave to me, since He gives me spirit and soul and bestows life upon me, so it is fitting that I cleave to Him" - and to this he says, "the love of his soul and his spirit," unqualified, which is a doubled love as we explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:18: This is what is written (Isaiah 26:9) "my soul desires You in the night" - my soul truly, for He, blessed be He, is the essence of the soul, since the lower soul is a single branch from the supernal root within it, and further, He truly is the soul - for without His vitality there is no soul. We find, then, that whoever loves his soul and spirit, repairing them through the performance of Torah and mitzvot, loves the Holy One, blessed be He - and from the affirmative you infer the negative.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 3:19: He says "in the night" - for a person, out of love of the Holy One, blessed be He, must rise every night. The matter of this love is like the parable of a man who loves his beloved: when he awakens at night, he is aroused by the yearning of love for her, and hastens to the occasion of his desire in great love, especially when he knows his beloved loves him. So too Torah scholars, who abstain from their wives all the days of the workweek because of the occasion of the King's daughter's desire, who is the Torah, should hasten in the yearning of Torah, for by engaging in it they cleave to the supernal life, and they cleave to the Shechinah, and she comes and bestows her holy spirit upon them. And the love of the Shechinah for us needs no proofs, for she says (Song of Songs 8:13) "you who dwell in the gardens, companions listen for your voice, let me hear it" - and this is why the prophet calls the Shechinah "my soul," and desires her, because she is the Holy Spirit that comes and rests upon him.
